paper_title: Drought in India: Its impact and mitigation strategies – A review

paper_identity.paper_title: Drought in India: Its impact and mitigation strategies – A review

paper_summary: This review synthesizes drought definitions, historical drought impacts, and mitigation strategies for India with emphasis on agricultural drought. It links deficient and erratic monsoon rainfall, dry spells, and high evapotranspiration to soil moisture stress, crop losses, and water-system stress. The paper highlights groundwater depletion under compensatory pumping and recommends watershed and water-use-efficiency-centered adaptation.
study_region: India (national review; includes drought-prone regions and multi-state examples)
study_period: Historical synthesis up to 2013; key drought examples include 1987, 2002, and 2009
methodology: Review article synthesizing published statistics, institutional reports, and agronomic drought-management evidence
paper_type_rationale: The paper aggregates prior evidence, definitions, and policy/practice recommendations instead of presenting a new single empirical causal model.

key_relationships: prec_annual_avg_rain, drysp_4w_trend, and et_annual_avg jointly reduce NEW_soil_moisture_index.
NEW_soil_moisture_index decline is linked with crop_yield_trend decline and cropping_area_trend contraction.
prec_annual_avg_rain decline reduces surface_water_area_avg, raising irrigation_demand.
Higher irrigation_demand accelerates g_annual_trend decline and contributes to deeper well_depth stress.
g_annual_trend decline is associated with higher salinity_level in groundwater.
NEW_water_use_efficiency is presented as a key adaptation lever that improves crop_yield_trend under scarcity.

mapping_notes: This is a review paper; many values are historical summaries and policy ranges rather than one harmonized modeled dataset. Extracted variables prioritize quantifiable constructs and drought mechanisms repeatedly emphasized in the text.
limitations: Causal effects are mostly qualitative and aggregated from multiple sources. Spatial and temporal comparability across cited studies is limited, so district/block implementation requires harmonized datasets and local validation.

important_variables.significance: Primary drought trigger used in definitions, classification, and historical impact narratives.
Core agronomic transmission variable linking climate anomalies to crop stress outcomes.
Major cross-stressor consequence of drought adaptation through pumping, with long-term sustainability implications.
Main food-system outcome with explicit large historical production losses cited.
One of the few mitigation variables tied to an explicit quantitative potential gain.

important_variables_narrative: The paper consistently treats rainfall deficit as the exogenous drought driver and root-zone moisture status as the immediate agronomic stress variable. Crop production losses are presented as the key measurable societal outcome. A critical cross-stressor pathway is drought-driven irrigation demand increasing groundwater depletion, which then propagates to well and water-quality stress. Among mitigation variables, improving water-use efficiency and expanding rainwater harvesting/watershed practices are emphasized as practical high-impact levers.
